ORIGINAL FINDING: The row's ONLY citation (identical for all 8 value fields, and identical to the citation on the sibling rows P7976/P7977/P7978, all last-touched 2026-03-15/16) is https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports_category/monthly/page/7/ -- a generic paginated CATEGORY-LISTING page ('Monthly Reports - Part 7 / September 2020'), not an article. url_verifier flags it explicitly: 'search/index page, not a document -- cite the underlying article or report, not a mutable navigation surface.' I fetched gem.wiki's own page for this pipeline and confirmed it cites nothing else. Per the standing rule, a row whose only support is a generic/aggregate citation that does not itself name the pipeline is an existence flag on its own. Independent search was constrained (WebSearch quota exhausted this session; Bing/DuckDuckGo returned unrelated/CAPTCHA pages via WebFetch), but I was able to fetch: (1) Arabic Wikipedia's 'Ras Shukheir' article (ar.wikipedia.org/wiki/راس_شقير, verified live, contains 'القاهرة'/'أنابيب') which states in general terms that crude is stored at Ras Shukheir and exported via a 36-inch pipeline and 'to Cairo via land-based petroleum pipelines' -- this corroborates that SOME real pipeline(s) run inland from Ras Shukheir toward Cairo, but the article itself is flagged as lacking citations, never names 'El-Hafair', and gives no length/diameter/capacity, so it cannot corroborate this row's specific segment or numbers, only the general concept that a corridor exists. (2) OpenStreetMap/Nominatim searches for 'El-Hafair' / 'Hafayer' / الحفاير / الحفير in Egypt returned NO matching place near the Suez/Gulf-of-Suez coastal route (only unrelated hits in Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Sudan, and Cairo-region street names) -- inconclusive on its own since small pump stations are often unmapped, but it means I could not independently geolocate the named endpoint either. Net: the broader idea of a Ras Shukheir-to-Cairo-area crude corridor is plausible and likely real (Ras Shukheir is a major, well-documented Gulf-of-Suez crude export/production hub), but THIS row's specific identity -- a discrete 'Ras Shukheir-El-Hafair' segment ending in Suez governorate, 215 km, 140,000 bpd -- rests on nothing but the sheet's own unverifiable generic citation and gem.wiki (itself sourced only from that same citation). This is a sourcing/verification failure, not a debunking -- I did not find evidence the pipeline is fictitious, only that it is currently unconfirmed by any source that actually names it.

REVISION (2026-08-27, batch QC): The source this finding asked for was found. The Sept-2020 EOG report's crude table names 'Ras Shukheir-Al Hafair' explicitly as one of the region's eight crude trunk lines, at 215 km / 26 in / 140,000 bbl/d -- matching the sheet on all three. The original finding's own suggestion (that 'El-Hafair' might be a mid-line pump station on a Ras Shukheir-to-Mostorod trunk rather than a line terminus) is REFUTED by the same table, which carries Ras Shukheir->Al Hafair, Al Hafair->Suez and Al Hafair->Mostorod as three separately itemised pipelines with different diameters (26 / 18 / 18-20 in). Al Hafair is a junction that is also a real line terminus. The existence flag was an artifact of the row's citation being the paginated index instead of the underlying article.
